name: code-writer-worktree-only-writes
body:
Code-writer agents — the core `implementer`, every `*-implementer`, and every `test-implementer` generated by the `agent-builder` — write only inside the project worktree they operate in (`<main>/apg/.worktrees/<project>/`). Reading main stays allowed.

The agent-builder template's grant rules are ROLE-AWARE: a code-writer's write grants (edit globs and the fs-tool path scope) live only under `apg/.worktrees/*/`; the corresponding repo-root paths stay denied (an explicit root deny is acceptable). Mirrored denies stay mirrored. The agent-builder itself holds its main `.opencode/agents/**` grant, and the optional `release-agent` holds its per-repo main release-artefact grants (it operates on main with a per-repo grant) — see `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`.

The fs tools (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) decide scope in ONE consistent frame: the granted globs and the candidate path resolve against the same root, so a worktree-rooted grant matches exactly the worktree path it names; a candidate path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is REFUSED for a code-writer whatever `directory` the caller passes. The grants and the decision function live in `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs` and `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision`. The mechanism is a plan-level choice (see the note on this requirement).

Acceptance criteria:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` states that code-writer write grants are worktree-only (`apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>`), that root paths stay ungranted to code-writers, and that the agent-builder and release-agent are the only generated/suite roles with main write grants; the ""Worktree mirroring"" bullet and rule 10 describe a worktree-only grant for code-writers.
- An `apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp` call by a code-writer whose (source or destination) path resolves into the main checkout is refused, whatever `directory` the caller passes; the same op on the matching worktree path inside the granted scope succeeds; a `..`/absolute escape stays refused; and a worktree path whose last matching `edit` entry is a `deny` is refused, mirroring `edit`.
- The opt-in suite e2e (`opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`) pins the main-refusal and the worktree-success cases, plus the deny-mirroring case (`requirements.note.fs-scope-deny-mirror`).
- Scope is product source only: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts`, `opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`, and `AGENTS.md`. The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts regenerated after this change releases: release a binary carrying the corrected template (product source embedded via `include_str!`) → install that released binary → re-run `apg init` (which installs the template into `~/.opencode/agents/`) → restart opencode → dispatch the agent-builder on main.
